question: Where was the first-ever International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Assembly held in India in June 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first-ever International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) Assembly** was held in **New Delhi**, India, in **June 2025**.
 
• The IBCA was established to protect and conserve **big cats** such as lions, tigers, leopards, cheetahs, jaguars, and snow leopards, which are facing threats due to habitat loss, poaching, and human-wildlife conflict.
 
• The assembly focused on building global cooperation to ensure the long-term conservation and survival of these majestic species.
 
• **New Delhi**, being the capital city of India, was chosen as the venue to emphasize India's commitment to wildlife conservation and its leadership role in the global conservation community.
 
• The event saw participation from member countries, conservation organizations, researchers, and policymakers aiming to strengthen partnerships and share best practices for big cat conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA):**

 
 
• The IBCA was launched as a global initiative by India to protect big cats, with a focus on **cooperative conservation efforts**.
 
• It aims to bring together countries and organizations working on big cat conservation under a unified platform to share knowledge, resources, and strategies.
 
• India has a rich legacy of big cat conservation, including iconic species like the Bengal tiger, Asiatic lion, and leopard.
 
 
 
• **Big Cats and Their Global Importance:**
 
 
• Big cats are apex predators and play a crucial role in maintaining the balance of ecosystems.
 
• Species like tigers, lions, and cheetahs are considered keystone species, meaning their presence ensures the health and stability of their habitats.
 
• Conservation of big cats also has a cultural and economic significance, as they attract ecotourism and are symbols of biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **India's Role in Big Cat Conservation:**
 
 
• India is home to several big cat species, including the **Bengal tiger**, **Asiatic lion**, and **leopard**.
 
• India has successfully implemented conservation programs such as **Project Tiger** (launched in 1973) and **Project Lion** to protect and increase the population of these species.
 
• India also reintroduced cheetahs in 2022 under the **Cheetah Reintroduction Project**, making it a global leader in wildlife conservation.
 
 
 
• **Global Threats to Big Cats:**
 
 
• Big cats face threats such as habitat loss due to deforestation, human encroachment, and urbanization.
 
• Illegal wildlife trade and poaching remain significant challenges, fueled by demand for big cat skins, bones, and other parts.
 
• Human-wildlife conflict is another major issue, particularly in areas where big cats and humans share close proximity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Conservation Efforts:**

 
 
• Organizations like the **World Wildlife Fund (WWF)** and the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** are actively involved in big cat conservation.
 
• Programs such as the **Global Tiger Initiative** and **Snow Leopard Trust** aim to conserve specific big cat species and their habitats.
 
 
 
• **India’s Conservation Milestones:**
 
 
• India hosts over **70% of the world’s tiger population** and has successfully increased their numbers through dedicated conservation efforts.
 
• The **Gir Forest National Park** in Gujarat is the last refuge of the Asiatic lion, and conservation efforts have helped stabilize their population.
